close_reason: Added an inline 'Do not remove this variant' defense note to AnniversaryDate::Unknown variant doc-comment, explaining the workspace extras-preservation rationale (future-spec @type values must round-trip losslessly) and cross-referencing the bead. The defense is visible on hover/cargo-doc, so a future contributor proposing removal will see the rejection before sending the PR. Tests pass; cargo doc -D warnings clean. Commit pending.
description: lib.rs:956-997 implements AnniversaryDate as a #[non_exhaustive] enum with PartialDate, Timestamp, and Unknown(serde_json::Value) variants, with a custom Serialize/Deserialize that dispatches on @type. The Unknown variant preserves any unrecognised @type shape opaquely so a Card carrying a future-spec date type round-trips losslessly through this crate. The test at :1486-1501 locks this behaviour in. This is the right shape: it matches the workspace 'extras-preservation' philosophy (preserve unknown fields rather than silently drop) and avoids forcing a major-version bump every time the IETF adds a new @type variant. A future contributor might suggest 'simplifying' by removing Unknown and falling back to a deserialize error — that would silently lose data for any spec-conformant input from a JSContact extension server, which is exactly the bug the variant exists to prevent. Defend Unknown against PRs to remove it.
title: AnniversaryDate::Unknown variant: forward-compat preservation of unknown @type values
